questions._flag: MEDIUM-SCOPED AWARD CLAUSE, and it runs in the direction that LEAVES THE ENGLISH KEY STANDING. This paper's marking scheme (55/5/3, Section-A row 16) prints the key '(A) Both Assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A)' and then, under a bold 'Note:', this verbatim clause: 'In Hindi version none of the answer is correct, so award one mark to each student who opted Hindi medium to write the answer.' READING TAKEN: the clause locates the fault in the HINDI edition and directs the compensating mark specifically at Hindi-medium candidates, which by exclusion leaves the English-medium candidate marked normally against the printed (A). We ingest the ENGLISH paper, so the row is NOT voided, `answer` stays (A), and `_cbseVoided` is deliberately NOT set — setting it would assert that CBSE voided a question it did not void for this edition. CORROBORATED DIRECTLY FROM THE SOURCE rather than inferred: this paper's own Hindi facing page (idx 9) prints the Hindi Assertion as 'किसी नैज अर्धचालक के प्रतिरोध में उसके ताप में वृद्धि के साथ वृद्धि होती है' — resistance INCREASES with temperature — the exact opposite of the English 'decreases'. That makes the Hindi Assertion FALSE while its Reason is TRUE, a combination the four printed codes do not offer at all (they run A-true/R-true/explains, A-true/R-true/does-not-explain, A-true/R-false, A-false/R-false), so the Hindi edition genuinely has no correct option while the English one is sound at (A). Both directions of the clause are therefore confirmed against the printed pages, not resolved by preference.

It is useful to design lenses of desired focal length using surfaces of suitable radii of curvature. This formula helps us obtain a relation between u, v and f for a lens. Lenses form images of objects and they are used in a number of optical devices, for example microscopes and telescopes.
questions.stem: Two convex lenses A and B of focal lengths 15 cm and 10 cm respectively are placed coaxially 'd' distance apart. A point object is kept at a distance of 30 cm in front of lens A. Find the value of 'd' so that the rays emerging from lens B are parallel to its principal axis.

questions.context: A capacitor is a system of two conductors separated by an insulator. The two conductors have equal and opposite charges with a potential difference between them. The capacitance of a capacitor depends on the geometrical configuration (shape, size and separation) of the system and also on the nature of the insulator separating the two conductors. They are used to store charges. Like resistors, capacitors can be arranged in series or parallel or a combination of both to obtain desired value of capacitance.
questions.stem: Find the equivalent capacitance between points A and B in the given diagram.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — the stem says only 'in the given diagram' and gives no circuit at all, so the drawing is the entire question. Described here: a capacitor network drawn between a terminal marked A on the left and a terminal marked B on the right, containing SIX capacitors, every one of them labelled C. DELIBERATELY WITHHELD: the topology — which capacitors lie in which branch and which nodes they join — since that is what the equivalent capacitance is computed from. Page idx 22.

questions.stem: Two slabs of dielectric constants 2K and K fill the space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate area A and plate separation d as shown in figure. Find an expression for capacitance of the system.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — the stem gives the plate area A, the separation d and the two dielectric constants, but NOT how the two slabs divide the space, and that division is printed only in the drawing. Described here: a rectangle representing the gap between the plates, split by a vertical line into a left region hatched with diagonal lines and labelled 2K and a right region hatched with horizontal lines and labelled K; a dimension line beneath the whole rectangle is labelled d, and two dimension lines above it label the widths of the two regions. DELIBERATELY WITHHELD: the two width labels themselves — they are the only thing fixing how the slabs share the separation and the expression cannot be written without them. Page idx 22.
